§3§lPurpose and mechanism§r
The Steam Fluid Drill produces a selected fluid; it is not an oil well. Output begins at a positive minimum and increases as efficiency builds. Its four modes are water, distilled water, brine and lava, with different output rates and steam costs. The mode switch is steel-tier only and resets efficiency. Use compatible pressure-steam input hatches; the structure does not impose a one-hatch maximum.

§3§lPreparation and operation§r
Choose the fluid you need before building for the intended tier and input route. Since efficiency increases during operation, repeated mode changes affect expected production; do not size storage and consumers solely around maximum output. Follow structure documentation for pressure-steam or ordinary input paths and provide a continuous outlet, updating the destination whenever the mode changes.
